reason: I'd tap 'Hard to sleep' at bedtime because it's free and I don't have to write anything. But $10 a month is a lot on my budget when free sleep sounds already knock me out.
objection: I don't want to type how I feel when I already feel bad, and the free sounds I use already work well enough.
would_change_my_mind: A one-tap bedtime session I could also play on my commute, at about $4 a month.

v1.why: A check-in form with notes every day is exactly what I don't want at bedtime.

v2.why: Skippable questions and the chips mean I can just tap and listen.

v3.why: Fine, though a journal and reports are more than I'll ever use for sleep.

reason: I'd try it between therapy sessions out of curiosity. My therapist and my own apps already cover this, so I don't see paying another $10.
objection: I don't want an app asking me questions every day; it starts to feel like homework.
would_change_my_mind: Something I could share with my therapist that actually made our sessions better.

v1.why: A daily check-in popping up when I sign in is the nagging I hate.

v2.why: Better, but 'How do you feel now?' after every session still feels like a question every time.

v3.why: Progress in words and the 'Why?' feel gentler and more like how my therapist talks.

reason: I'm not letting an AI write a script about my mental health. When a deadline gets to me I put on a YouTube breathing video I already trust, and it's free.
objection: I already have free apps and YouTube for this, and I don't trust AI-made content on something this personal.
would_change_my_mind: Scripts reviewed by a named clinician, with that shown clearly in the app.

v1.why: It opens on someone else's conversation with sleep scores; that feels made up.

v2.why: Cleaner, but it's still an AI deciding what I should hear.

v3.why: The 'Why?' on each change is the most honest part, but not enough for me to trust it.

reason: I paid for Headspace, used it for three weeks and cancelled, so I know how I work. I'd poke at the free tier, but I'm not paying again until I've actually stuck with it.
objection: I don't want an app asking me questions every day, and I know I'll drop it after a month like last time.
would_change_my_mind: Still opening it every week after two months of free use, then a cheap annual deal.

v1.why: Daily check-in plus coins everywhere: same churn I had before.

v2.why: 'Chapter 2 is ready tomorrow' is a streak by another name; I'd fall off it.

v3.why: Low pressure, and a report every two weeks is about my speed. Maybe.

reason: I'm on my phone in bed anyway, so I'd try one free sleep session. A few free a day covers all I'd ever use, and YouTube rain sounds are fine with the kids waking me up regardless.
objection: I already have free apps and YouTube for this, and the free tier already gives me enough.
would_change_my_mind: If it actually stopped me scrolling and got me asleep faster for a couple of weeks running.

v1.why: Menu, coins, a check-in form: too much to deal with at 11pm.

v2.why: Simple tabs, one question and play; works half asleep.

v3.why: Same as 2, but a journal and wearable questions are things I'll never touch.

reason: I'd sign up on day one, and if the first session sounds good, $10 is nothing next to what I spend on apps. I'd pay just to get every voice and longer sessions to show friends.
objection: I don't want to type how I feel when I already feel bad; if the chips and voice input don't cover it, I'll stop.

v1.why: Opening on someone else's chat and coins everywhere feels like a prototype.

v2.why: The onboarding and my own first chapter make it feel made for me.

v3.why: The 'Why?' and the private journal are what I'd tell people about.

reason: I already pay for Oura and a meditation app, so money isn't the issue. I'd only switch if it showed me my HRV or sleep actually changing, and nothing in the pitch promises that.
objection: I already have free apps and YouTube for this, and what I pay for already shows me data.
would_change_my_mind: Live Oura data showing a measurable change in my sleep or HRV after its sessions.

v1.why: The percentages look like sample numbers, not my numbers.

v2.why: It has numbers at least, but they aren't tied to my ring.

v3.why: It asks about my wearable, then takes away numbers and tells me in words. That's backwards for me.

reason: Free, sure, I'd make a session before a big meeting once or twice. I've never paid for one of these and I'm not starting with $10 a month.
objection: Another subscription I'll forget to use.
would_change_my_mind: A one-off purchase of a session pack instead of a subscription.

v1.why: The coin counter feels like it's working up to selling me something.

v2.why: Fine, but YouTube is already open on my laptop.

v3.why: Nicest of the three, but it doesn't change my free-only habit.

reason: I'd try it before a stressful week and check my Watch afterwards. If my stress readings don't move, it's a gimmick and I won't pay.
objection: Will it actually help, or is it a gimmick?
would_change_my_mind: Seeing my Apple Watch heart rate or HRV drop after sessions, inside the app.

v1.why: 'Score improved by 7%' on someone else's chat makes me trust it less.

v2.why: The percentages look like sample data, not proof.

v3.why: The wearable option and 'Why?' answer my gimmick question, if they're real.

reason: A synthetic voice reading a script made up about my feelings is a bit creepy to me. When I'm stressed I'd rather have a real person's guided meditation.
objection: AI-made meditation sounds generic or a bit creepy.
would_change_my_mind: A free sample I can hear before signing up that sounds like a real, warm human voice.

v1.why: Opening on 'Good morning, Adam' with someone else's sleep score is the creepy part.

v2.why: Less cluttered, but the core problem is still the AI voice.

v3.why: Calmer, and the wearable stays off until I choose, but I still wouldn't listen.
